blocks.text: Jenny reached the roof in her pink suit and white mask. Seth was waiting beside the stairwell in his orange uniform. He had changed at home and hurried over. The steel drum stood where they had left it, its blackened patch facing the wall.
“Anything?” Jenny asked.
Seth shook his head. “Not yet.”
They went to the parapet together. Jenny searched the sky to the left, above the lower roofs. Seth looked the other way, toward a thin bank of clouds.
“There.” He raised his brown-gloved hand and pointed.
blocks.alt: On the rooftop in full superhero uniforms, Jenny stands in side profile looking left across the sky while Seth, viewed from behind, points right toward an approaching bright orange object above Cleveland. Jenny wears her pink suit, white mask, gloves and boots; Seth wears orange with white accents and brown gloves and boots.

blocks.text: A bright orange point moved above the buildings to their right. It grew larger as it approached, until Jenny could make out the face inside the flames. She let out a breath she had been holding.
Flaming Head swept over the parapet and stopped before them.
“Ready?” he asked.
“We need to talk first,” Jenny said.
He looked from her to Seth. “What happened?”
Jenny told him about Eleanor’s promise: free electricity for Cleveland, from a source she would not name. Seth explained why they suspected Daniel.
“He used Perch to run the robot,” Seth said. “Now she’s promising enough power for the whole city.”
“And you think he wants mine.”
Jenny nodded. Flaming Head’s bright expression faded. His eyes lowered toward the roof, and the flames curled more slowly around his face.
blocks.alt: On Jenny’s apartment roof, costumed Jenny and Seth talk with Flaming Head, whose lowered eyes and thoughtful expression show concern about Daniel extracting his energy.

blocks.text: “Perch got his power from you,” Seth said. “Could Daniel take enough from you to do that?”
“I don’t know how much he could take.” Flaming Head looked up. “I saw what he was doing to Perch. He kept drawing energy out while Perch fought to get free.”
“Billy says we can’t rush into the lab,” Jenny said. “We don’t know what Daniel’s building.”
“I wanted to go,” Seth admitted. “Fist did, too.”
Flaming Head drifted nearer the parapet. Below them, windows caught the late afternoon light. Someone was calling a child in from the street.
“If people need electricity, I’d like to help,” he said.
Jenny stepped closer. “That’s different from Daniel putting you in a machine.”
“I know.” He turned back toward her. “You’re right to warn me.”
Seth’s hands tightened against the brick. He loosened them before the edge began to crumble.
“We won’t let him take you.”
Flaming Head studied his face. “You don’t have to watch the sky every minute, Seth. I can watch for him, too.”
“What if he sends Luke?”
“Then I’ll keep away from him.”
“And the laboratory,” Jenny said.
Flaming Head nodded. “I won’t go there alone.”
For a little while they stayed beside the wall. Seth kept glancing toward the rooftops until Flaming Head followed his gaze.
“Shall we practice?”
Seth looked at him. “Now?”
“That’s why we came.”
They moved the drum into the practice space. Seth checked that Jenny was clear before lifting it. Halfway up, he heard a clatter below and turned his head. The drum tilted.
He caught it, lowered it and stood still.
“Again?” Jenny asked.
Seth looked toward the street, then back at the drum. “Again.”
This time he finished the lift before looking away. The base touched the roof squarely.

Jenny chose the scorched patch for her target. Her first attempt faded when she looked past it toward the skyline. She stopped, settled her feet, and tried once more. The small plasma ball struck the steel with a sharp flare.
Flaming Head watched from beside the stairwell. His familiar warmth reached them, but his smile remained quieter than usual.
When they finished, Jenny asked where they could find him if they learned anything more.
“I’ll stay near here,” he said. “Or Billy’s window.”
Seth left the drum upright beside the wall. “And you’ll tell us if Daniel comes looking?”
“I will.” Flaming Head rose a little above the parapet. “If he wants my help, he can ask.”
Seth looked at Jenny. Neither thought Daniel would ask.
